- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially > -0.5) — reduce forecast by 5–10% in such regimes.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >+1.5% from prior day) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- Forecast mean reversion too aggressively when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — avoid sharp downward corrections.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are over-predicted — adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day lagged sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive after a downtrend, forecast should not overshoot — cap upward revisions at +1.0% from prior day’s close.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment volatility — smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 sentiment values before adjustment.
